title: Introduce rolling SLO grace-window and connection mellowing to reduce churn during transient overloads
author: Aisha Kumar
commits: 9f3b2a8 - Introduce RollingGraceWindow type and core logic
b1e4c7d - Add connection mellower hook and backpressure smoothing
c8d5e01 - Autoscaler: emit warmup hints and respect grace window
a2b7f66 - Add integration tests for transient overload and warmup
d4f8e2b - docs: describe observability and recommended SLO settings
release_notes: Adds a rolling SLO grace window and a connection mellowing component to reduce aggressive tenant eviction during short-lived overloads. Improves stability for bursty workloads; no customer API changes. Suggested config: slo.grace_window_ms=15000 for regional fleets; enable via feature flag 'rolling_slo_grace'.
description:
Context: We observed several incidents where short-lived latency spikes (20s–2m) caused the SLO enforcer to transition tenant circuits into aggressive eviction, producing large numbers of reconnects and KV-cache churn. This made recovery slower and increased p99 tail for steady traffic once load normalized.

Motivation: introduce a conservative, rolling grace window that lets short spikes decay without immediate hard eviction and add a connection ‘mellower’ that gently paces connection draining to avoid head-of-line eviction cascades.

High-level design:
- Rolling SLO grace window: sliding time window per-tenant that accumulates transient violations and only escalates to eviction if the weighted violation score exceeds threshold within the window. Configurable decay and weight by route.
- Connection mellowing: when a tenant is marked for soft-evacuate, instead of immediate connection termination, the mellower stages connections through drain states with exponentially increasing backoff for new requests.
- Autoscaler integration: autoscaler emits warmup hints when ramp activity is detected and the grace window is active; the scheduler prefers soft capacity adjustments before invoking hard eviction.
- Observability: new metrics (slo_grace.score, connection_mellower.active, slo_grace.escalations) and two new alert rules to detect prolonged grace-window escalations.

Checklist:
- [x] Core logic implemented and unit-tested
- [x] Integration tests covering transient spike and sustained overload
- [x] Autoscaler hooks wired and validated in simulator
- [x] Telemetry dashboards + alerts updated
- [x] Feature flag gated rollout (rolling_slo_grace)

Implementation notes: commits summarized below; most changes are behind the 'rolling_slo_grace' feature flag. Configuration changelog in pkg/config/feature_flags.go. Files changed (high-level): serving/runtime/shedder/rolling_grace_window.go - core algorithm and unit tests; serving/runtime/connection/mellower.go - connection state machine and drain pacing; serving/runtime/alloc/autoscaler.go - emit warmup hints and respect grace scoring; console/telemetry/alerts.yaml - two alerts tuned to 15m windows; tests/integration/soft_evacuate_test.py - end-to-end scenario with synthetic spike; docs/observability/rolling-slo.md - guidance for operators; pkg/config/feature_flags.go - feature flag and defaults.

Tests & CI:
- Unit test coverage added for scoring and mellow transitions.
- Integration test sim simulates a 45s spike that previously caused full-eviction; with this change the tenant experiences a controlled soft-evacuate and recovers without client reconnect storms.
- CI initially failed on a flaky test in tests/integration/soft_evacuate_test.py due to timing sensitivity; added deterministic clock and re-ran; final CI: passed (all checks green).

Review conversation (condensed):
- Tomás: "Can the grace-scoring be gamed by a tenant sending microbursts?" Reply: "We weight violations by CPU/latency magnitude and include a decay term; microbursts produce limited score because sustained resource usage is required to cross threshold. Added unit tests demonstrating a 2s microburst does not escalate."
- Lena: "Ensure observability so SREs can differentiate grace-window usage vs genuine overloads." Reply: "Added slo_grace.escalations and connection_mellower.active metrics + dashboard doc."
- Ben: requested smaller default window for low-latency fleets; reply: "Added per-fleet override and sane default 15s. Documented in docs/observability/rolling-slo.md."

Approval & merge: After addressing timing flakiness and documenting per-fleet config, reviewers approved. Squash-merged into main on 2026-01-20.

Rollout: gated behind feature flag; staged rollout to 10% of regional fleets for 48h, monitor slo_grace.escalations and p99 latency.

Post-merge followup items:
- Monitor for false positives on low-TPS tenants and consider a minimum-sample requirement
- Add a lighter-weight approximate scorer to reduce memory overhead for large tenant counts
